name: tasks
description: Ordered task list for the coordinator's own planning state. Persisted on the coordinator workstream so it survives restarts. Use to decompose work, mark progress, and link tasks to spawned children via `child_ws_id`. Actions: `add` (append), `update` (mutate title/status/child_ws_id/note by id), `remove`, `reorder`, `list`. Statuses: `pending`, `in_progress`, `done`; `blocked` = something you may be able to clear yourself is in the way; `needs_user` = only a user decision/approval/grant can proceed - a valid place to stop; say what you need in `note`. Titles and notes over 200 chars are rejected rather than truncated. `child_ws_id` is a free-form label, not validated against the workstreams table (pre-spawn placeholders and post-close references are legal).

action.description: One of: add / update / remove / reorder / list.

title.description: For 'add' and 'update': task title. Max 200 chars; longer titles are REJECTED (not truncated).

status.description: For 'add'/'update': pending / in_progress / done / blocked / needs_user. `blocked` = a dependency you may be able to clear yourself (a build, a sibling task, a running child). `needs_user` = waiting on a decision, approval, or grant only the user can give; pair it with `note`.

note.description: For 'add'/'update': optional one-sentence note - say what you need from the user on a `needs_user` task (setting status does not overwrite the title). Max 200 chars; longer is REJECTED. Empty string on 'update' clears it.

child_ws_id.description: For 'add' and 'update': optional free-form ws_id label. NOT validated against the workstreams table — the coordinator owns the linkage semantics (pre-spawn placeholders and post-close references are both legal).

task_ids.description: For 'reorder': new ordering by task_id (must be a permutation of existing task_ids).
